title: "Reproducible NGS Data Analysis"
subtitle: "RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, containers, Git, and public sequencing data"

# Welcome

Modern sequencing projects require much more than running bioinformatics tools.

A reproducible analysis requires:

```text
metadata retrieval
-> raw data retrieval
-> workflow execution
-> design-specific analysis
-> documentation
-> version control
```

This workshop introduces a practical workflow for organizing, executing, documenting, and interpreting RNA-seq and ChIP-seq analyses using public datasets and lightweight computational infrastructure.

The practical examples focus on bacterial genomes and small datasets that can be explored on personal laptops, while introducing concepts that can also scale to larger projects and institutional computing environments.

::: {.callout-important}
This workshop teaches a reproducible approach to RNA-seq and ChIP-seq analysis using public sequencing datasets, containers, Git/GitHub, and structured project documentation.

Rather than focusing on a single software package, the workshop emphasizes workflows that can be understood, reproduced, shared, and adapted to real research projects.

The goal is to give you practical experience with the core steps of reference-based NGS analysis and to provide a project framework that you can reuse in your own research or laboratory work.
:::

***

# Learning objectives

By the end of the workshop, you should be able to:

- Create a reproducible NGS project structure
- Use Git and GitHub to document analyses
- Use Docker containers to run bioinformatics tools
- Retrieve public sequencing datasets from SRA, ENA, and ArrayExpress
- Generate and interpret quality-control reports
- Perform basic RNA-seq and ChIP-seq analyses
- Produce differential expression and peak-calling results
- Associate regulatory regions with nearby genes
- Document and communicate results through reports and figures

***

# What students will build

Students do **not** clone a finished analysis repository or copy a hidden template.

Instead, each participant progressively creates their own GitHub repository containing:

- a clear project structure
- metadata tables
- analysis scripts
- selected reports
- figures
- workflow documentation

By the end of the workshop, each student should have:

1. A reproducible GitHub repository
2. A documented RNA-seq and/or ChIP-seq workflow
3. A short report summarizing the analysis

The assembly of this repository will be used to evaluate student progress.

***

# Datasets

The workshop uses publicly available datasets derived from small bacterial genomes.

The main examples are based on *Helicobacter pylori* strain N6 datasets generated to study the HP1021 redox switch regulon under microaerophilic and aerobic growth conditions:

- *Helicobacter pylori* RNA-seq: `E-MTAB-13025`
- *Helicobacter pylori* ChIP-seq: `E-MTAB-13026`

These datasets are associated with the publication:

Noszka M. et al. "Profiling of the *Helicobacter pylori* redox switch HP1021 regulon using a multi-omics approach." *Nature Communications* (2023).

- Publication: [PubMed Central](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10593804/) and [Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-42364-6)
- RNA-seq dataset: [E-MTAB-13025](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress/studies/E-MTAB-13025?key=bf2d8677-1b26-4f1e-ac5f-b1c78c7590be)
- ChIP-seq dataset: [E-MTAB-13026](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress/studies/E-MTAB-13026?key=2b27b413-e118-4802-859e-5da57ff1ead2)

The full study includes multiple conditions and analyses. In this workshop, we focus on a small teaching subset of the wild-type strain under microaerobic and aerobic conditions.

Our small teaching workflow captures the logic of the published analysis, but it is simplified for laptop-scale execution. It should not be interpreted as a full reproduction of the paper.
